advances: Finite preservation for positive planar raw data under both endpoint cap ceilings. The geometric statement requires actual fixed chords and the stated signed sector changes.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
For positive data, $\sum_i f_i\sqrt{q_i}=2$. At a tight row $i$ with all rows at most two put $x=f_i$, $z=\sqrt{2-x}$, $g=f_j+f_l=2z$, $F=x+g=3-(z-1)^2$, and $C=x+g^2/2=2+z^2$. The cap ceiling and moment give $F\ge2/\sqrt{128/279}>7379/2500$ since $4/(128/279)-(7379/2500)^2=85093/12500000$. Hence $39/50<z<61/50$. Each row inequality is equivalent to $[f_s-(F-2)]^2\le4(3-F)$. Together with $f_j+f_l=2z$ this bounds either nonselected entry by $z^2-2z+2$ for $z\le1$ and by $4z-z^2-2$ for $z\ge1$.

Each upper bound is strictly less than $4z/(2+z^2)=2g/C$. To check this, multiply by $2+z^2$ and subtract $4z$. On the lower interval the polynomial is $z^4-2z^3+4z^2-8z+4$, with increasing derivative (second derivative $12z^2-12z+8>0$), derivative $-2$ at one, and value $-2408459/6250000$ at $39/50$. On the upper interval it is $-z^4+4z^3-4z^2+4z-4$, with positive derivative $4[1-z(z-1)(z-2)]$ on $[1,61/50]$ and value $-159641/6250000$ at $61/50$.

Write $e_i=x$ and $e_s=gf_s/2$ for $s\ne i$ so that $\sum_s e_s=C$, and set $T_s=1/\sqrt{q_s}$. Logarithmic differentiation of $f_s$ gives the row's negative derivative $\alpha_s$ for a unit loss from $k,Q_s$:
$$2k\alpha_s=C+e_s T_s^2-Cf_s T_s.$$
The minimum of the quadratic in $T_s$ is $C-x C^2/4=C(2-x)^2/4>0$ when $s=i$. Otherwise it is $C-C^2 f_s/(2g)>0$ by the nonselected bound.

For gains, the same squared row inequalities give each nonselected entry a lower bound $4z-z^2-2$ on the lower interval and $z^2-2z+2$ on the upper interval, using the upper bound on the other entry and their sum on the latter interval. In particular every entry, including $x=2-z^2$, is at least $1279/2500$. As $\sqrt{128/279}<17/25$ and $F\le3$, the moment gives
$\sqrt{q_s}>17/25-1/(25f_s)\ge17/25-100/1279>3/5$.
Also $\sqrt{q_s}<7/10$, so $10/7<T_s<5/3$. The unit gain missed by cap $s$ increases $k$ and both $Q_j$ with $j\ne s$. Its derivative $\beta_s$ satisfies
$$2k\beta_s=C+\sum_{j\ne s}(e_jT_j^2-Cf_jT_j).$$
Each summand is convex in $T_j$, so endpoints $T_j\in\{10/7,5/3\}$ suffice for an upper bound. If $s=i$, a bound is the maximum over these two choices of $P=C+2z(zT^2-CT)$. If $s\ne i$, write $L=4z-z^2-2$ on the lower interval and $L=z^2-2z+2$ on the upper interval. For the included nonselected entry use $f_j\ge L$, since $zT-C<0$ for either endpoint $T$ by $2+z^2-5z/3>0$. The bounds are then the maximum of $P=C+(2-z^2)(T_1^2-CT_1)+L(zT_2^2-CT_2)$ over the four endpoint pairs.

For completeness, for each such polynomial $P$ and interval $[a,b]$ expand $-P(a+(b-a)u)=\sum_{k=0}^n c_ku^k$. Its degree-$n$ Bernstein coefficients are $B_j=\sum_{k=0}^j c_k\binom jk/\binom nk$. This follows by expanding each $u^k$ against the Bernstein basis via the binomial theorem. Substituting the two stated endpoint choices in these coefficient sums gives:

| Choice | Minimum on $[39/50,1]$ | Minimum on $[1,61/50]$ |
|---|---:|---:|
| $T=10/7$ | $441821/612500$ | $73/49$ |
| $T=5/3$ | $4959/6250$ | $13/9$ |
| $(T_1,T_2)=(10/7,10/7)$ | $6347669/7656250$ | $386711/612500$ |
| $(T_1,T_2)=(10/7,5/3)$ | $3197731/3750000$ | $308439211/551250000$ |
| $(T_1,T_2)=(5/3,10/7)$ | $368112407/551250000$ | $374439739/551250000$ |
| $(T_1,T_2)=(5/3,5/3)$ | $972313/1406250$ | $136669/225000$ |

The basis is nonnegative and sums to one, and all minima exceed $1/2$. Thus every $\beta_s<-1/(4k)$.

The transfer path stays positive by interpolation. Its cap ratios are fractional-linear functions with positive denominators, so each stays between its endpoint values. At a common feasible boundary every tight row has derivative $-\sum_s E_s\alpha_s+\sum_s G_s\beta_s<0$ for a nonzero transfer. Initially tight rows immediately become strict and initially strict rows stay strict for a short interval. At a first later contact with the boundary, including at $t=1$, a tight row would have nonnegative left derivative. This is impossible. Zero transfer leaves the rows unchanged.

For the geometric consequence, assign each $E_i$ to the actual loss of unique area in cap $i$ and each $G_i$ to the actual gain of double area missed by cap $i$. The sector partition gives the exact displayed changes of total and cap areas, and the common chords give common coarea lengths $\sigma_i$. For a strict distinct-vertex triangle, on each original edge the third margin is negative, so the zeros of the other two occur in the order that makes their positive intervals overlap. The six-ray hull leaves three disjoint vertex corners, each in its unique sector. Thus the indicated inner body keeps all chords and changes only unique areas. The hypotheses of 33488d4938a6ee4a hold at $T$, giving the initial rows. A proper compact convex inner body has strictly smaller area by separating an omitted point and using the nonempty interior of $T$.
statement:
For positive data $k,Q_i,\sigma_i$, $i=1,2,3$, set $q_i=Q_i/k$, $M=\sum_i Q_i/\sigma_i$, $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_i M)$, and $\Phi_i=f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4$ for $\{i,j,l\}=\{1,2,3\}$. For $E_i,G_i\ge0$, put $E=\sum_i E_i$ and $G=\sum_i G_i$. Keep the sections fixed and set $k(t)=k(0)+t(G-E)$ and $Q_i(t)=Q_i(0)+t(G-G_i-E_i)$ for $0\le t\le1$. Suppose both endpoints have positive data and all their cap ratios satisfy $q_i\le128/279$. If the initial rows are all at most two, the final rows are all at most two, strictly below two if any transfer is nonzero. At a tight row on the common feasible boundary in this cap band every unit unique loss has strictly negative derivative, and every unit double gain has derivative less than $-1/(4k)$.

For actual planar bodies with common interior mark, balanced spanning cap normals and identical full cutting chords, the transfer hypotheses hold if each final unique-sector area is no greater and each final double-sector area is no smaller. In particular, if $T$ is a strict distinct-vertex triangle, $C_T$ is the hull of its six cutting-ray endpoints, and $C_T\subseteq K\subseteq T$, the result applies when both $T$ and $K$ have the stated cap ceiling. The rows are strict for $K\ne T$.
title: Finite planar Lorentz-row preservation under unique losses and double gains
